scripts.name: tk-top-ips
scripts.title: Busiest addresses
scripts.what: Counts every IP address in a file, busiest first.

scripts.name: tk-failed
scripts.title: Failed sign-ins
scripts.what: Finds failures and denials, then shows which addresses caused them.
scripts.src:
[ -n "$1" ] || { echo 'Give a file, for example: tk-failed auth.log'; exit 2; }
f="$1"
t=/tmp/.tk-failed
grep -iE 'fail|invalid|denied|unauthori|TCP_DENIED|" 40[13] |/40[13] ' "$f" > "$t"
echo "$(wc -l < "$t") failure lines in $f"
grep -oE '([0-9]{1,3}\.){3}[0-9]{1,3}' "$t" | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -n 10
rm -f "$t"

scripts.name: tk-by-minute
scripts.title: Activity by minute
scripts.what: Draws a bar for each minute, so bursts stand out.
scripts.src:
[ -n "$1" ] || { echo 'Give a file, for example: tk-by-minute auth.log'; exit 2; }
awk '{if($1~/^[0-9]{10}(\.[0-9]+)?$/)t=strftime("%H:%M:%S",int($1));else if(match($0,/[0-9][0-9]:[0-9][0-9]:[0-9][0-9]/))t=substr($0,RSTART,RLENGTH);else if(match($0,/[0-9][0-9]:[0-9][0-9]/))t=substr($0,RSTART,RLENGTH);else next;print substr(t,1,5)}' "$1" | sort | uniq -c | awk '{c[NR]=$1;t[NR]=$2;if($1>m)m=$1}END{for(i=1;i<=NR;i++){n=int(c[i]*40/m);if(n<1)n=1;b="";for(j=0;j<n;j++)b=b"#";printf "%s %5d %s\n",t[i],c[i],b}}'

scripts.name: tk-between
scripts.title: Lines in a time window
scripts.what: Keeps only the lines between two times.
scripts.src:
[ -n "$3" ] || { echo 'Give a file, a start and an end, for example: tk-between auth.log 09:00 10:00'; exit 2; }
awk -v a="$2" -v b="$3" '{if($1~/^[0-9]{10}(\.[0-9]+)?$/)t=strftime("%H:%M:%S",int($1));else if(match($0,/[0-9][0-9]:[0-9][0-9]:[0-9][0-9]/))t=substr($0,RSTART,RLENGTH);else if(match($0,/[0-9][0-9]:[0-9][0-9]/))t=substr($0,RSTART,RLENGTH);else next;if(t>=a&&substr(t,1,length(b))<=b)print}' "$1"

scripts.name: tk-status
scripts.title: Web status codes
scripts.what: Counts the HTTP status codes in a web or proxy log.
scripts.src:
[ -n "$1" ] || { echo 'Give a web or proxy log, for example: tk-status access.log'; exit 2; }
grep -oE '" [1-5][0-9]{2} |/[1-5][0-9]{2} ' "$1" | grep -oE '[1-5][0-9]{2}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn

scripts.name: tk-timeline
scripts.title: Merged timeline
scripts.what: Merges every line that starts with a full date into one timeline, oldest first.
scripts.src:
d=${1:-.}
find "$d" -type f ! -name "*.pcap" | sort | while IFS= read -r p; do
    grep -E '^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}[ T][0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}' "$p" 2>/dev/null | sed "s|\$|   [$(basename "$p")]|"
done | sort | head -n "${2:-60}"

scripts.name: tk-iocs
scripts.title: Pull out indicators
scripts.what: Lists the addresses, domains, links, hashes and emails found in a folder.
scripts.src:
d=${1:-.}
show() { echo "== $1"; grep -rhoE "$2" "$d" 2>/dev/null | sort -u | head -n 40; }
show Addresses '([0-9]{1,3}\.){3}[0-9]{1,3}'
show Links 'https?://[^ "<>]+'
show Domains '[a-zA-Z0-9-]+(\.[a-zA-Z0-9-]+)*\.(com|net|org|io|xyz|ru|cn|top|info|biz|co|in|edu|lan|local)\b'
show Hashes '\b[a-f0-9]{64}\b'
show Emails '[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+@[a-zA-Z0-9.-]+'

scripts.name: tk-check-bad
scripts.title: Check against a bad list
scripts.what: Hashes each file and looks for it on a threat intel list.
scripts.src:
[ -n "$1" ] || { echo 'Give a folder, for example: tk-check-bad suspect known_bad.txt'; exit 2; }
d="$1"
[ -n "$2" ] || { echo 'Give the list of bad hashes, for example known_bad.txt'; exit 2; }
l="$2"
find "$d" -type f | sort | while IFS= read -r p; do
    h=$(sha256sum "$p" | cut -d" " -f1)
    if grep -q "$h" "$l"; then echo "KNOWN BAD   $p"; else echo "not listed  $p"; fi
done

scripts.name: tk-hash-all
scripts.title: Hash all evidence
scripts.what: Writes a SHA-256 manifest, so you can prove later that nothing changed.

scripts.name: tk-verify
scripts.title: Verify the manifest
scripts.what: Checks every file against the manifest and names anything that changed.
scripts.src:
sha256sum -c "${1:-/tmp/evidence.sha256}" 2>&1 | grep -v ": OK$"
if sha256sum -c "${1:-/tmp/evidence.sha256}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "Every file matches."; else echo "Some files changed or are missing."; exit 1; fi

scripts.name: tk-preserve
scripts.title: Pack a preserved copy
scripts.what: Packs the case folder into an archive and prints its hash for your notes.
scripts.src:
n=${1:-evidence}
tar cf "/tmp/$n.tar" -C "$HOME" case
ls -l "/tmp/$n.tar"
sha256sum "/tmp/$n.tar"

scripts.name: tk-sweep
scripts.title: Find live hosts
scripts.what: Sweeps a network range on the case network and lists who answers.

scripts.name: tk-ports
scripts.title: Open ports and services
scripts.what: Scans one host on the case network for open ports and services.

scripts.name: tk-domain
scripts.title: Look up a domain
scripts.what: Shows a domain's address and who registered it.
scripts.src:
[ -n "$1" ] || { echo 'Give a domain, for example: tk-domain example.com'; exit 2; }
n="$1"
echo "== Address"
dig +short "$n"
echo "== Registration"
whois "$n"

scripts.name: tk-talkers
scripts.title: Who talked to whom
scripts.what: Summarises the conversations in a capture.

scripts.name: tk-dns-queries
scripts.title: DNS names asked for
scripts.what: Counts the domain names looked up in a capture. Tunnels show up as odd, long names.
scripts.src:
f=${1:-capture.pcap}
tshark -r "$f" -Y dns -T fields -e dns.qry.name | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -n 30

scripts.name: tk-http
scripts.title: Web requests in a capture
scripts.what: Lists each web request: who asked, which site and which page.
scripts.src:
f=${1:-capture.pcap}
tshark -r "$f" -Y http.request -T fields -e ip.src -e http.host -e http.request.method -e http.request.uri | head -n 40

scripts.name: tk-decode
scripts.title: Try common decodings
scripts.what: Tries Base64, hex and ROT13 on a string, so you can spot the readable one.
scripts.src:
[ -n "$1" ] || { echo 'Give some text, for example: tk-decode aGVsbG8='; exit 2; }
s="$1"
echo "base64: $(printf %s "$s" | base64 -d 2>/dev/null)"
echo "hex:    $(printf %s "$s" | xxd -r -p 2>/dev/null)"
echo "rot13:  $(printf %s "$s" | tr 'A-Za-z' 'N-ZA-Mn-za-m')"
